cohort: 380 pregnant women admitted for delivery with hemoglobin <11 g/dl, who were well-nourished (Mid-Upper Arm Circumference > 21cm and Body Mass Index 18.5-24.9)
finding: Maternal hemoglobin deficiency was statistically significantly associated with birth weight, gestational age, and mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate was higher (71.1%) compared to normal vaginal delivery (28.9%) among anemic mothers.
